item.title: Missing Australian hiker Jordan Yap last seen on remote trail found dead in Peru
item.description:
Family and friends say Melbourne man should be remembered for ‘immense joy he brought to so many people’s lives’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australian trekker who was last seen on a remote South American hiking trail has been found dead, his family have said.

Jordan Yap, 30, last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.

item.title: ‘It was a terrible thing’: Panama declares state of emergency as quake aftershocks rattle communities
item.description:
More than 100 aftershocks as high as magnitude-5.8 recorded after two quakes toppled buildings and prompted evacuations

Panama’s government has declared a state of emergency on Saturday as the aftershocks of two powerful earthquakes that roiled the country shook communities for hours.

Officials did not attribute any deaths to Friday’s 7.7- and 6.6-magnitude earthquakes, but reported damages in all 10 of Panama’s provinces and two Indigenous territories.

item.title: Marina Silva on Flávio Bolsonaro: He will try to finish his father’s ‘perverse project’ to destroy the Amazon
item.description:
Exclusive: Former Brazilian environment minister warns of destruction as far-right scion favourite to become president

The former Brazilian environment minister Marina Silva has said that if Flávio Bolsonaro becomes president he will seek to finish the “perverse project” of rampant rainforest destruction initiated by his jailed far-right father.

The Amazon was thrown into chaos during Jair Bolsonaro’s 2019-2022 presidency, when Brazil’s environment and Indigenous protection agencies were gutted and environmental criminals ran riot, causing surges in deforestation and violence.

item.title: Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
item.description:
Leftwing Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores beats far-right candidate in election in remote district of Andes

A businessman called Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores has been elected the mayor of a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, according to local election data.

The 45-year-old, who shares two of his names with the notorious European dictators, won the race for mayor of Queropalca, in Peru’s central Huánuco region, and will take office on 1 January.

item.title: A mudslide sweeps away cars and a bus in Santiago after the wettest October on record
item.description: A torrent of water, mud and rocks swept away cars and a public transport bus on Thursday in San Carlos de Apoquindo, in the Las Condes district at the foot of the Andes in eastern Santiago, Chile, after a week of record rainfall. The official toll is six injured, with no deaths or missing, and President José Antonio Kast has declared a disaster zone in the district.

item.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro wins support of third-place candidate in presidential race
item.description: Brazil's right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro secured third-place finisher Augusto Cury's endorsement on Thursday, strengthening his position against incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ahead of the runoff. Cury won nearly three percent in Sunday's first round. A Datafolha poll put Bolsonaro ahead with 52 percent against Lula's 48 percent.

item.title: How the UK's Online Casino Regulation Has Become a Global Reference Point
item.description: The United Kingdom's approach to regulating online gambling has attracted significant attention from policymakers, industry observers and player advocacy groups outside its borders. item.title: Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take
item.description:
Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take

Two years after Ismael Zambada Garcia, alias "El Mayo," was handed over to US authorities in what was deemed a traitorous act by one faction against another, the war between the Chapitos and the Mayiza factions of the Sinaloa Cartel continues to roil the area. The conflict has implications for the criminal superstructure throughout the country.

InSight Crime's Victoria Dittmar and co-director Steven Dudley were recently in Culiacán, Sinaloa, where they interviewed drug producers, residents, and local sources. They found a city where the war is less visible than it was but no less present.

The post Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take appeared first on InSight Crime.
